subject: nineTailedKitsune
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: nine-tailed kitsune fox with spirit flames.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a reasonably sized module using the agentic-3js-builder API, making sure to correctly use its joint, chain, sweep, part, stick, surface, decal, cards, along, and ring functions alongside paint, svg, animeEye, and glow utilities.

Keeping the module around 400-500 lines, I'm sketching the fox's scale and pose: a standing quadruped roughly 1.4m long with nine tails fanning out from the rump, each tipped with spirit flames rendered via glow cards. I'm working through the joint hierarchy starting with a hips root joint, then building a spine chain using a catmull path connecting hips to chest to neck base, and considering how to sweep the body geometry along that spine path with a radius function tied to the bone.

Still building the skeleton...

Simplifying with nested spike cones for the flame tips, maybe adding a flame texture card as an alternative, then moving to positioning the head joint.

Now I'm figuring out the facial structure: a scaled sphere for the snout, mirrored ear shapes, cheek spheres, and eye decals placed on a slightly flattened spherical head.

For the legs, I'm planning to use limb() calls for each of the four legs, setting shoulder and hip positions, paw targets on the floor, segment lengths, and bend directions for the joints.

I need to check leg reach: parenting paws to hips/chest joints and verifying segment lengths actually span the distance to the ground targets, adjusting lengths like 0.42/0.4 so the limb can reach without overextending.

Now I'm setting a tapering ellipse radius function along the spine for the body sweep, sizing the hip-to-chest span, and deciding on a cream/orange toon-shaded fur material using the toon kit.

For tails I'm setting up a gradient that shifts into an indigo tip band near the end, keeping the body otherwise matching the coat color. I'll skip extra accessories like ribbons or bells to stay focused on the fox itself, and plan to use decal textures for the eyes and a flame-like texture detail.

I'm writing an SVG flame shape with layered cyan and white paths for a glowing effect, and confirming the glow helper works directly on the cards mesh array. Now I'm working out the tail placement math, positioning the hip joint and spreading multiple tails across an azimuth angle range before building out each tail's curve.

Writing tail positioning math...

Defining tail geometry and flame effects...

Adding orbiting flame positions around the tail, then moving to head geometry—defining a head joint with its parent, position, and aim point, plus a neck curve built from catmull-rom control points connecting chest to head.

Working through the joint hierarchy, I'm deciding to keep hips as the root joint slightly offset from the spine's starting point so the spine1 joint isn't coincident with it, avoiding zero-length segments while keeping the chain structure simple.

I'm planning the limb parenting: front legs attach to the spine2 joint (the second entry in the spine chain) while hind legs attach to hips. Now I'm setting up the head sphere geometry with eye placement, positioning it relative to the head bone with a slight upward and forward offset.

Placing muzzle and nose spheres at fixed literal offsets, then working out eye placement using surface azimuth/elevation hits on the head mesh for symmetric positioning.

Still working out ear geometry...

Right—I need the ear plane spanned by the forward/back axis and up axis instead, so it faces sideways like a real ear. Reworking the outline direction vectors to use z for the outline axis and y for up, with a slight x tilt for the mirrored ear.

Defining the triangular ear outline shape, then setting up the fur-edge coat material with orange and cream tones and a subtle teeth pattern along the edge.

Now I'm working out paint functions for the tail with an indigo tip and the legs with a lighter sock color near the paw, nesting these color decisions based on position along the body.

I'm also considering decorative decals: eyes, nose, maybe a small forehead rune or gem, and a glow effect for the flame elements. Then I'm starting the actual module imports for the build, pulling in the builder, frame, rng, limb, and curve utilities from the SDK.

Writing character build code...

Defining the neck sweep bone...

Setting up the leg chains with named hip/knee/paw joints, then attaching a scaled ellipsoid paw to the chain's tip bone.

I'm coloring the legs with a paint function so socks fade from cream to coat tone, then checking the hip and shoulder joint distances for hind and front legs to make sure the limb reach fits—the front legs come out slightly too long, so I'll need to adjust.

Working out the head position and sizing, then computing the nine tail chains branching from the hip point with sine/cosine curves for a fanned fox-tail spread.

Finishing the tail sweep with a tapering radius, then positioning flame cards at the tail tip using a frame oriented upward so they stand correctly.

I'm also adding glow meshes around the cards, and placing several small floating flame orbs at scattered positions around the body for extra flair, checking that they don't violate the "nothing floats above" constraint since they're part of the subject itself.

For the eyes, I'm grabbing the head's surface and finding hit points near the front to place decals with mirrored positioning for left/right symmetry, guarding against null hits. Then I'm starting on the muzzle as a small cream-colored sphere part.

Adding muzzle details...

Simplifying this — instead of a separate inner ear shape, I'll just paint the ear with a function that colors the tip indigo and the base as coat color based on the y-coordinate of the extrude profile.

I'm also placing a small gold gem on the forehead using a sphere geometry, and defining the head itself as a slightly flattened sphere with coat coloring positioned above the body.

I'm skipping extra mouth details and relying on the spine sweep for the chest. I still need to handle card frame textures and glowing spirit orbs, using the flame SVG texture and glow kit for emissive effects, while keeping tail colors nested through the paint function.

Now I'm defining a leg-building function that computes limb joint points, creates a bone chain with hip/knee/paw names, sweeps the leg geometry with a tapering radius, and adds a paw sphere at the foot target, making sure hips are the root joint before legs.

Defining hind leg positions and bends...
